name: Fondazione Pastificio Cerere
overview: Non-profit contemporary art foundation at Via degli Ausoni 7 in the San Lorenzo district of Rome, in a former pasta factory.

The Cerere pasta factory was founded in San Lorenzo in 1905 and supplied pasta and flour to the city until 1960. From the early 1970s artists, later known as the San Lorenzo group, took studios in it (the foundation's history page).

The Fondazione Pastificio Cerere was founded in 2005, and its headquarters opened in the building with the exhibition "RESIDENTI". Flavio Misciattelli, who took a room in the building in 1998 on his family's property, is its president (the foundation's history and governance pages).
funding_verdict: Fondazione Pastificio Cerere (Rome): donor-funded with public project grants: private gifts plus Ministry of Culture, SIAE and Ministry of the Interior money for specific shows

name: Museo Nazionale Etrusco di Villa Giulia
overview: The Museo Nazionale Etrusco di Villa Giulia is a national museum in Rome whose stated mission is to promote its collections and Etruscan culture and to lend works to Italian and international exhibitions (museum website).
The museum also manages the Parco Archeologico di Veio (museum website).

What is there: the site singles out the Lamine di Pyrgi, the Testa di Leucotea, the Sarcofago degli sposi, the Apollo di Veio, the Scudo bilobato and the Tomba François, a painted tomb from Vulci now permanently displayed there (museum website). The pages read gave no object count.
funding_verdict: Museo Nazionale Etrusco di Villa Giulia: state-funded national museum, topped up in 2023 from another museum's takings.

name: Fondazione Merz
overview: A centre for contemporary art at Via Limone 24, Turin, in a 1930s industrial building in Borgo San Paolo, the former Officine Lancia power station (foundation website).
Established in 2005 and named after Mario Merz; the Turin project was designed with him according to the biography of Beatrice Merz (foundation website).
What is there: it alternates exhibitions on Mario and Marisa Merz with site-specific projects by other artists (foundation website).
funding_verdict: Fondazione Merz: private and public mix, donors plus region, a bank foundation and Compagnia di San Paolo.

name: PAV - Parco Arte Vivente
overview: Experimental contemporary art centre at Via Giordano Bruno 31, Turin, built on the relationship between art and nature, with an open-air exhibition site and an interactive museum on art, biotechnology and ecology (PAV website; City of Turin notice, 2025).

Conceived by the artist Piero Gilardi (Finestre sull'Arte, 9 June 2020). The City of Turin notice cites a city executive deliberation of 15 March 2005 on the complex. The association acPav ran the project (Artribune, Helga Marsala, 13 January 2014). The PAV website names Enrico Bonanate as director.
The first environmental installation, "Trèfle" by Dominique Gonzalez-Foerster, dates from 2006 (PAV website).
funding_verdict: PAV, Parco Arte Vivente: mainly public: City of Turin and Regione Piemonte

name: Palazzo Madama
overview: The city's old fortress, later renovated into a palace and institutional residence, in Piazza Castello, Turin, listed as a UNESCO World Heritage site (museum website).
It belongs to the Fondazione Torino Musei network with GAM and MAO, together with the Art Library and Photo Archive (museum website).
What is there: the Museo Civico d'Arte Antica; the page read gives no collection size (museum website).
funding_verdict: Palazzo Madama: public, the city of Turin plus two banking foundations and the region, through Fondazione Torino Musei.

name: Fondazione Giorgio Cini
overview: A private cultural foundation and study centre on the island of San Giorgio Maggiore in Venice, in the former Benedictine monastery, which it holds on a concession in use (foundation profile; statute, article 22).
Created in 1951 by Vittorio Cini in memory of his son Giorgio, who died in an air crash on 31 August 1949; the restoration of the island was written into its aims (foundation profile).

What is there: an endowment that the statute lists as buildings, works of art, collections, libraries, furniture and industrial shares and bonds, first given by the family of Count Vittorio Cini and added to by bequests and donations (statute, article 3); research institutes for art history, music, theatre and literature (Intesa Sanpaolo website). The pages read gave no count of works of art.
funding_verdict: Fondazione Giorgio Cini: private, an endowment from the Cini family plus yearly contributions from two banks' groups, an insurer and an energy company

name: Miho Museum
overview: The Miho Museum is at 300 Momodani, Tashiro, Shigaraki, Koka, Shiga, in the mountains, and the page title describes it as a museum designed by I.M. Pei (museum website).
It opened in November 1997 and Takeshi Umehara was its first director; the Shumei Culture Foundation runs it (museum website, history page).

What is there: Mihoko Koyama (1910 to 2003) started the collection, which holds Japanese art and ancient art from Egypt, Western Asia, Greece, Rome, Southern Asia and China; the pages read give no object count (museum website, history page).
funding_verdict: Miho Museum: run by the Shumei Culture Foundation; the pages read state no funding

name: Chichu Art Museum
overview: A museum built underground on the island of Naoshima, Kagawa, so as not to disturb the Seto Inland Sea panorama, designed by Tadao Ando (museum website; Japan Tourism Agency text, mlit.go.jp).

It opened in July 2004 as part of Benesse Art Site Naoshima, whose origins the site traces to Tetsuhiko Fukutake, founding president of Fukutake Publishing, and Chikatsugu Miyake, then mayor of Naoshima (Benesse Art Site Naoshima history page).

What is there: permanent works by three artists, Claude Monet's Water Lilies series shown in natural light, James Turrell, including Open Sky, and Walter De Maria (museum website; mlit.go.jp). Soichiro Fukutake chose three artists so that each work has room (The Peak, 22 December 2016).
funding_verdict: Chichu Art Museum: private, a family foundation funded from Benesse shares, plus tickets

name: Gotoh Museum
overview: Private art museum at 3-9-25 Kaminoge, Setagaya-ku, Tokyo, five minutes' walk from Kaminoge station on the Tokyu Oimachi line (museum website).
It opened on 18 April 1960 as a private foundation museum, planned by Gotoh Keita (1882 to 1959), who laid the foundations of the Tokyu Group and died shortly before it opened (museum website).

Collection: Japanese and East Asian art Gotoh collected over half his life, starting with Nara-period sutra copies, then Zen calligraphy and tea utensils; he bought the collection of Takanashi Nisaburo, including the Genji handscroll, and ancient mirrors from Moriya Kozo (museum website).
funding_verdict: Gotoh Museum: corporate foundation: mainly donations from Tokyu Corporation

name: Okura Museum of Art
aliases: Okura Shukokan Museum of Fine Arts
overview: The Okura Museum of Art is on the fifth floor of The Okura Tokyo, in front of the main hotel entrance, at 2-10-4 Toranomon, Minato-ku (museum page on the hotel website).
Industrialist Kihachiro Okura established it in 1917; it is Japan's oldest existing privately operated museum (museum page on the hotel website).

What is there: about 2,500 pieces including ceramics, paintings, calligraphy, sculptures and samurai armour; three National Treasures, 13 works of important cultural property status and 44 important works of art; the 10th-century Kokin Wakashu poetry collection is a highlight (museum page on the hotel website).
funding_verdict: Okura Museum of Art: private: an industrialist's foundation museum inside a hotel; the pages read give no accounts

name: teamLab Borderless
aliases: teamLab Borderless: MORI Building DIGITAL ART MUSEUM
森ビル デジタルアート ミュージアム：エプソン チームラボボーダレス
overview: A ticketed digital art venue by the art collective teamLab in an underground space of the Azabudai Hills development in Minato City, Tokyo (Tokyo Updates, 7 April 2023; Good Luck Trip listing).
teamLab created Borderless in 2018; it opened in Odaiba in June 2018, closed at the end of August 2022 and reopened at Azabudai Hills on 9 February 2024 (Tokyo Updates; Time Out Tokyo).

What is there: immersive digital artworks by teamLab alone; Guinness World Records named the Odaiba venue in 2019 the world's most visited museum dedicated to a single art group, and it drew approximately 2.3 million visitors from over 160 countries and regions in its first year (Tokyo Updates, 7 April 2023).
funding_verdict: teamLab Borderless: commercial, a developer's venue paid by ticket sales

name: Adachi Museum of Art
overview: Art museum with Japanese gardens at 320 Furukawa-cho, Yasugi, Shimane Prefecture (museum website).
Founded in 1970 by Adachi Zenko (1899 to 1990), then aged 71, in the village where he was born, to thank his hometown and support culture in Shimane (stated by the museum).

The collection holds about 2,000 works, with about 120 by Yokoyama Taikan at its core (Japanese Wikipedia). In 1979, after about two years of negotiation, Adachi bought several Taikan works from the Kitazawa Collection, among them "Autumn Leaves" (museum website).
funding_verdict: Adachi Museum of Art: private: a public interest foundation built on its founder's business fortune, with paid admission

name: Yokohama Triennale
overview: The Yokohama Triennale is a contemporary art exhibition held in Yokohama and organised by the Organizing Committee for Yokohama Triennale (triennale website).
The first edition was Yokohama 2001: Mega Wave; the City of Yokohama took over organisation from the Japan Foundation in 2011 (triennale website).

What is there: the 8th edition ran from 15 March to 9 June 2024, the first in spring; the 9th is announced for 23 April to 12 September 2027 (triennale website). It holds no permanent collection in the pages read.
funding_verdict: Yokohama Triennale: public and partner funded; the pages read give no amounts

name: Darat al Funun (The Khalid Shoman Foundation)
overview: Arts centre ("a home for the arts") in Jabal al Weibdeh, Amman, with its main entrance at 13 Nadeem al Mallah Street, on a 5,196 square metre compound overlooking downtown Amman (stated by the space).

Founded by the artist Suha Shoman, who from 1988 hosted exhibitions and lectures on contemporary Arab art at the Scientific and Cultural Center of the Abdul Hameed Shoman Foundation. Darat al Funun opened in 1993 (Sarah Rogers, Darat al Funun essay, 2013). Restoration of the current site began in 1992 and the Main Building opened in 1993 (stated by the space).
Came under the Khalid Shoman Foundation in 2002. The third house was renamed Dar Khalid in memory of the patron Khalid Shoman (stated by the space).
funding_verdict: Darat al Funun: private non-profit initiative: founded and led by Suha Shoman, under the Khalid Shoman Foundation
wider_context: Arab Bank: on 22 September 2014 a jury in the US District Court, Eastern District of New York, found the bank liable for knowingly supporting terrorism relating to 24 terrorist acts (Linde v. Arab Bank). On 9 February 2018 the US Court of Appeals for the Second Circuit overturned the verdict, finding that the District Court failed to give the jury adequate instructions (Wikipedia).

Arab Bank: in 2005 the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network assessed a $24 million penalty against its New York branch for failing to implement an adequate anti-money laundering programme (Wikipedia).

The Star says Khalid Shoman, son of the bank's founder, joined the bank's board in 1957 and was Vice-Chairman from 1974 until June 2001. Rogers calls him Darat al Funun's patron and deputy chairman of the Abdul Hameed Shoman Foundation, whose Scientific and Cultural Center hosted Suha Shoman's exhibitions from 1988, before Darat al Funun opened in 1993. Wikipedia says Arab Bank created that foundation in 1978.

name: Kuona Collective
overview: Artist-run collective and studio centre in Kilimani, Nairobi. Wikipedia states that Kuona Artists Collective was established in Kilimani in 2017 following the closure of Kuona Trust.

A New York Times piece reposted by Ginanne Brownell says the Kuona Trust closed in September and the Collective opened in December on the same grounds, as an artist-run space where artists offer studio space, art open days and residencies.

The National Museums of Kenya page lists the Kuona Artists Collective among its galleries as Kenya's oldest contemporary art centre, founded in 1995, with dedicated studios, exhibitions, residencies, workshops and mentorship for emerging artists.
funding_verdict: Kuona Collective: artist-run space on the grounds of the former Kuona Trust

name: Casino Luxembourg – Forum d'art contemporain
overview: Contemporary art centre at 41 rue Notre-Dame in Luxembourg City's Ville Haute, founded in 1996. It presents exhibitions mostly by younger international artists (Casino Luxembourg).
Kevin Muhlen is director general and Ruta Franke deputy director (Paperjam).

Building: opened in 1882 as the Casino Bourgeois, designed by Pierre and Paul Funck, where Franz Liszt gave his last piano recital in July 1886. After the State bought it in 1959 it became the Foyer Européen and a glass and steel pavilion by René Maillet was added (Wikipedia).
funding_verdict: Casino Luxembourg: funded by the Ministère de la Culture, in partnership with Les Amis des Musées d'Art et d'Histoire Luxembourg

name: Museo Franz Mayer
aliases: Museo Franz Mayer de Artes Decorativas
overview: Museo Franz Mayer occupies a 16th-century building in the historic centre of Mexico City that belonged to the Order of San Juan de Dios and was a hospital until 1966 (museum website).
It is a trust whose Patronato was established by the German-born philanthropist and collector Franz Mayer; the pages read did not state the opening year.

What is there: the Colección Franz Mayer plus five more collections, Ruth D. Lechuga, Wolfgang Paalen, William Spratling, Marguerite Rostan and Robert Everts (museum website). The museum says it has conserved Mayer's books, paintings and decorative arts for about 40 years.
funding_verdict: Museo Franz Mayer: private trust administered by Banco de México, with donations and memberships

name: Mediamatic
overview: Art and science foundation at Mediamatic Biotoop, Dijksgracht 6, 1019 BS Amsterdam, in Dijkspark within walking distance of Central Station (Mediamatic).
Founded in 1983 in Groningen and moved to Amsterdam in 1986. In 1983 its focus was media technology (Mediamatic history page). Mediamatic.net went online in 1994 (Mediamatic history page).

Founders Willem Velthoven and Jans Possel stepped back from their active roles in 2024 after four decades. Marcel Sturing is the new general director, and Velthoven stays involved in 2025 as his coach (annual report 2024, translated).
funding_verdict: Mediamatic: subsidy-funded: Stimuleringsfonds Creatieve Industrie and Amsterdams Fonds voor de Kunst (AFK), with earned income of 28% in 2024

name: OT301 (Vereniging EHBK)
overview: Collectively run, not-for-profit venue at Overtoom 301, 1054 HW Amsterdam, combining housing, workspaces and public functions for arts, politics and subculture (OT301 website).

Squatted in 1999 by a group of activists and artists called Eerste Hulp Bij Kunst (EHBK, "First Aid for Art"). The group later paid rent and bought the building in 2006 (The Amsterdammer, Elitsa Kaleva, 22 January 2023). Wikipedia says the building was the former Dutch film academy and that EHBK bought it from the council.
Runs as the association Vereniging EHBK, organised as a "horizontal democracy" (The Amsterdammer, 2023).
funding_verdict: OT301: association-owned: a building bought by its users' association, with city money for a green roof

name: Sonic Acts
overview: Interdisciplinary arts organisation in Amsterdam, founded in 1994 to support new developments in electronic and digital art. It runs a biennial international festival combining art, theory and technology, and the Sonic Acts Academy for artistic research (Sonic Acts).

Wikipedia says it was founded by Paradiso and the ArtScience Interfaculty, which included the Royal Academy of Art and the Royal Conservatory of The Hague, and that the festival was originally held each year at Paradiso.

The 2026 Biennial, "Melted for Love", ran from February to March 2026 with 80 events at 20 venues in Amsterdam, including Muziekgebouw, Paradiso, the Stedelijk Museum, W139, Framer Framed, Arti et Amicitiae, Rozenstraat and Zone2Source in Amstelpark (Subbacultcha; Re-Imagine Europe).
funding_verdict: Sonic Acts: supported by an EU programme, a Dutch arts fund, the Amsterdam arts fund and Paradiso
